title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: exclude specific domains from web grounding

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the briefing overstates domain exclusion as a complete citation block, although Microsoft says news and other answer verticals may still be cited. It also gives incomplete governance paths, describes a policy-creation command as a web-search block, and makes unsupported licensing and agent-applicability claims.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is rolling out.
claims.quote: "status": "Rolling out", "statusKey": "rolling-out"

claims.claim: The roadmap gives September 2026 as the General Availability date.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2026"
claims.fix: Change 'with a September 2026 General Availability date' to 'with General Availability targeted for September CY2026'; the status is still Rolling out.

claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.claim: The roadmap provides no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Listed sites must not be used or cited in web-grounded answers.
claims.quote: Currently, domain exclusions support filtering on web page results only. Results from other answer verticals, such as news, might still be cited.
claims.fix: Qualify the summary and body: domain exclusion filters web page results, not every answer vertical; news and other verticals might still cite excluded sites. Do not present it as a comprehensive citation or acceptable-use block.

claims.claim: Cowork honours the organization's domain exclusions.

claims.claim: No exclusion configuration exists by default; an administrator opts in by running the script.
claims.quote: Default settings don't include the domain exclusion configuration. Opt in to use the feature by running the PowerShell script.

claims.claim: The correct default-state classification is off.
claims.quote: Default settings don't include the domain exclusion configuration. Opt in to use the feature by running the PowerShell script.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to admin-opt-in. The standard assigns that value to a new control that restricts nothing until an administrator configures it.

claims.claim: A Search Administrator or Global Administrator can run the script.
claims.quote: Sign in as a Search Administrator or Global Administrator.

claims.claim: The script requires the Az.Accounts module.
claims.quote: Az.Accounts PowerShell module (the ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 script installs the module automatically if it's missing).

claims.claim: The script can be run with an appropriate Copilot or Global admin role.
claims.quote: Sign in as a Search Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.fix: Replace 'appropriate Copilot or Global admin role' with 'Search Administrator or Global Administrator', matching the control-row note and the feature prerequisites.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no admin UI for domain exclusion.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusions admin center UI Cloud Policy configuration. Opened Domain exclusion overview and Configure Microsoft Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center; only the script was documented.

claims.claim: The exclusion list is not visible in Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "domain exclusion" Copilot "Cloud Policy" visibility. Opened domain-exclusion, configure-copilot-admin-center and overview-cloud-policy; none states whether the list is visible there.
claims.fix: Replace the visibility assertion with 'Microsoft documents domain exclusion management through the PowerShell script at the time of writing (November 2026).'

claims.claim: The exact Microsoft 365 Apps admin center path is Cloud Policy > Allow web search in Copilot.
claims.quote:
Under Customization, select Policy Management.
On the Policy configurations page, select Create.
claims.fix: Use 'Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow web search in Copilot'. Cite overview-cloud-policy for navigation and manage-public-web-access for the setting; the existing docs link alone gives no such path.

claims.where: controls[1].scope, note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Allow web search in Copilot controls Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat for users or groups across the tenant.
claims.quote: This policy allows IT admins to either turn on or turn off web search for users or user groups across the tenant they manage

claims.where: controls[1].note; What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The policy can enable web search, disable it, or disable it only in work mode.
claims.quote:
Enabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat
Disabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat
Disabled in Microsoft Copilot Work mode; Enabled in Microsoft Copilot Web mode and Microsoft Copilot Chat

claims.claim: No equivalent API or automation call is documented for the Allow web search in Copilot Cloud Policy setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Allow web search in Copilot Cloud Policy PowerShell Graph API. Opened manage-public-web-access and overview-cloud-policy; no equivalent PowerShell or Graph configuration call was documented.

claims.claim: The Purview path goes directly from Custom to the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location.
claims.quote:
Select the Custom template, then Custom policy.
On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
claims.fix: Insert 'Custom policy > Locations' after 'Custom'. To make this a web-search blocking control, continue with 'Content contains > Sensitive information types' and 'Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches', then save and turn on the policy.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <name> -Locations <location> -EnforcementPlanes @('CopilotExperiences') implements the sensitive-content web-search control.
claims.quote: The fourth command creates the DLP policy using the $loc variable for the value of the Locations parameter, and "Copilot Policy" as the name of the policy (use any unique name).
claims.fix: The cmdlet, Name, Locations and EnforcementPlanes parameters, and CopilotExperiences value are real, but this creates only a policy container. Label it 'policy creation only; a sensitive-information rule and Performing Web Searches action must also be configured', rather than claiming equivalence to the blocking control.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Purview DLP can block external web search when a prompt contains configured sensitive information types.
claims.quote: When a user prompt contains the configured SITs, Copilot and Cowork block external web search as a grounding source and continue to generate the response using allowed internal Microsoft 365 data sources.

claims.claim: A Copilot DLP policy can be tenant-scoped.
claims.quote: An unrestricted administrator can scope policies to administrative units or keep Full directory to apply a policy across the organization.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: When enabled, web grounding sends a derived search query to the search provider and uses web content in responses.
claims.quote: Based on these terms, Copilot generates a search query that it sends to the Bing search service asking for more information.

claims.claim: Web grounding sends a derived query, not Graph data.
claims.quote: Copilot finds the name of the user's manager from Microsoft 365 data. It then generates a Bing search query based on their name to see what information about them is available on the web.
claims.fix: Replace 'not Graph data' with 'not entire Microsoft 365 files; generated search terms can be informed by organizational data, including document content or a manager name'. Keep the distinction between derived queries and full prompts/files.

claims.claim: Prompts leave the tenant unless the Purview DLP web-search action stops them.
claims.quote: The user's prompts and Copilot's responses are stored within Microsoft 365 and never leave the service boundary for both Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat without customer direction.
claims.fix: Say 'Domain exclusion filters incoming web results; it does not prevent generated search queries being sent to Bing. Purview DLP can block external web search when prompt text matches configured sensitive information types.' Do not equate generated queries with full prompts.

claims.claim: Users will not be told why a site was not cited.
claims.quote: Searched: "domain exclusion" "notification" Copilot; Copilot domain exclusion declarative agents scoped web search users notification excluded domains. Opened domain-exclusion and manage-public-web-access; neither documents exclusion notifications.
claims.fix: Remove the assertion or write 'Microsoft has not documented user messaging for domain exclusions at the time of writing (November 2026).' The recommendation to publish the policy internally can remain as advice.

claims.claim: Wildcard-style blocking of whole top-level domains is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "domain exclusion" "wildcard" Copilot. Read the full domain-exclusion page, including CSV format and limitations; no whole-TLD wildcard syntax was documented.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Domain exclusion is included and requires no additional licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion licensing additional license cost metered; "domain exclusion" "license" Copilot. Read domain-exclusion prerequisites and licensing search results; none states domain exclusion is included or needs no additional licence.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to unknown. Replace 'No additional licence' and 'No licence' with 'Feature-specific licensing is not yet published; the documented script prerequisites name roles, PowerShell and CSV requirements but no licence.'

claims.claim: Domain exclusion has no metered cost.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion licensing additional license cost metered. Read domain-exclusion and returned licensing excerpts; none states domain exclusion is unmetered or free.
claims.fix: Replace 'No licence or metered cost' with 'Feature-specific licensing and pricing are not yet published; no domain-exclusion meter is documented at the time of writing (November 2026).'

claims.claim: The cost classification is none because configuration uses a script.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion licensing additional license cost metered; "domain exclusion" "license" Copilot. The roadmap and domain-exclusion page do not state inclusion in existing licences; script-based configuration is not pricing evidence.
claims.fix: Set cost to low and use 'Low. Maintaining the CSV and running the script take administrator time; feature-specific licensing and pricing are not yet published.' The standard reserves none for documented inclusion in licences already held.

claims.claim: Web search is off by default in government clouds.
claims.quote: By default, web search is enabled for Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat in commercial tenants, but not for U.S. Government Community Cloud (GCC, GCC-High, and DoD) tenants.

claims.claim: Government clouds are not listed for this roadmap item.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: Scope: third bullet; Open questions: agent interaction
claims.claim: Tenant domain exclusions do not apply to declarative agents' scoped web search.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion declarative agents scoped web search users notification excluded domains; "domain exclusion" "declarative". Read domain-exclusion and knowledge-sources web-search excerpt; neither documents that exemption.
claims.fix: Remove 'Does not apply to'. Say 'Declarative agents can scope web search in their manifest; Microsoft has not documented how tenant domain exclusions interact with those scoped sites.' This also agrees with the existing open question.

claims.claim: Declarative agents can scope web search to sites configured in their manifest.
claims.quote: To scope your web search to specific sites, add the sites property and specify up to four URLs, as shown in the following example.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/knowledge-sources#web-and-scoped-web-search to sources and cite it for the scoped-web-search background, not for any domain-exclusion exemption.

claims.claim: Copilot > Settings > Data access links to web-search policy configuration in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.
claims.quote: Follow the link from Copilot settings to create an Allow web search in Copilot cloud policy in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: Users retain a personal web-search toggle when administrative policy permits web search.
claims.quote: If the IT admin turns on web search for Microsoft Copilot users, those users still have the option to turn off web search by using the Web content toggle.

claims.claim: Microsoft presents domain exclusion as part of its prompt-defense protections.
claims.quote: Domain exclusion | Administrators can use a PowerShell script to exclude up to 1,000 sites from web grounding in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Medium impact is justified by changing the sources every Copilot user may see once configured.
claims.quote: impact: "medium"; impact: Medium. Changes what web sources every Copilot user may see cited once configured.
claims.fix: Align the impact rationale with the scale: use high if most users are expected to notice tenant-wide exclusions, or retain medium with a specific explanation of the limited affected population. Do not justify medium with 'every Copilot user'.

claims.claim: Feature-specific government cloud availability remains unpublished.
claims.quote: Searched: "domain exclusion" Copilot government GCC availability. Read domain-exclusion and government-availability search excerpts; no feature-specific government availability was stated, and the roadmap lists only Worldwide.
